text:
Trent Frederic, 28, has one goal in 23 games and no points in his last 21, and our numbers don't call it bad luck: he had about 3.3 points of expected production over that stretch, and the chances have thinned out too. He plays under 10 minutes a night in the bottom six, and his 58 hits are the most visible part of his game.

Some of it is finishing. His 2.16 individual expected goals (the quality of his own chances) say he's about a goal light, and he's shooting 4.8%, under the 8.7 to 13.4% range we'd expect from him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season had him on the end of good passes, 1.6 shots per 60 off feeds across the slot or from behind the net, which is where his goals should come from.

The five-on-five share is the bigger problem. The Oilers get 35.5% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than 12 points worse than without him, and they've scored 3.0 more goals than those chances deserve, so the results flatter him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and under Mike Babcock his minutes aren't guaranteed.
